<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino: * Iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino: * Iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro:
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino: * Iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino: * Iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino: * Iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, exsultémus Dómino: * Iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro.
b.fb8d173c76:
<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Let us adore the Lord * He is our Creator.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us adore the Lord * He is our Creator.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us adore the Lord * He is our Creator.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> He is our Creator.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us adore the Lord * He is our Creator.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> He is our Creator.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us adore the Lord * He is our Creator.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> He is our Creator.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us adore the Lord * He is our Creator.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
Incipit liber Daniélis Prophétæ
<r>Dan 1:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> Anno tértio regni Ióakim regis Iuda, venit Nabuchodónosor, rex Babylónis, in Ierúsalem et obsédit eam:
<n>2</n> Et trádidit Dóminus in manu eius Ióakim, regem Iuda, et partem vasórum domus Dei: et asportávit ea in terra Sénnaar in domum dei sui, et vasa íntulit in domum thesáuri dei sui.
<n>3</n> Et ait rex Asphenez præpósito eunuchórum, ut introdúceret de fíliis Israël, et de sémine régio et tyrannórum,
<n>4</n> Púeros, in quibus nulla esset mácula, decóros forma, et erudítos omni sapiéntia, cautos sciéntia, et doctos disciplína, et qui possent stare in palátio regis, ut docéret eos lítteras et linguam Chaldæórum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Vidi Dóminum sedéntem super sólium excélsum et elevátum, et plena erat omnis terra maiestáte eius:
* Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.
<r>℣.</r> Séraphim stabant super illud: sex alæ uni, et sex alæ álteri.
<r>℟.</r> Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the book of Daniel
<r>Dan 1:1-4</r>
<n>1</n> In the third year of the reign of Joakim king of Juda, Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, and besieged it.
<n>2</n> And the Lord delivered into his hands Joakim the king of Juda, and part of the vessels of the house of God: and he carried them away into the land of Sennaar, to the house of his god, and the vessels he brought into the treasure house of his god.
<n>3</n> And the king spoke to Asphenez the master of the eunuchs, that he should bring in some of the children of Israel, and of the king's seed and of the princes,
<n>4</n> Children in whom there was no blemish, well favoured, and skilful in all wisdom, acute in knowledge, and instructed in science, and such as might stand in the king's palace, that he might teach them the learning, and the tongue of the Chaldeans.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and the whole earth was full of His glory;
* And His train filled the temple.
<r>℣.</r> Above it stood the Seraphim each one had six wings.
<r>℟.</r> And His train filled the temple.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>Dan 1:5-7</r>
<n>5</n> Et constítuit eis rex annónam per síngulos dies de cibis suis, et de vino unde bibébat ipse, ut enutríti tribus annis, póstea starent in conspéctu regis.
<n>6</n> Fuérunt ergo inter eos de fíliis Iuda, Dániel, Ananías, Mísaël, et Azarías.
<n>7</n> Et impósuit eis præpósitus eunuchórum nómina: Daniéli, Baltássar; Ananíæ, Sidrach; Misaéli, Misach; et Azaríæ, Abdénago.
<r>Dan 1:8-10</r>
<n>8</n> Propósuit autem Dániel in corde suo, ne polluerétur de mensa regis, neque de vino potus eius: et rogávit eunuchórum præpósitum ne contaminarétur.
<n>9</n> Dedit autem Deus Daniéli grátiam et misericórdiam in conspéctu príncipis eunuchórum.
<n>10</n> Et ait princeps eunuchórum ad Daniélem: Tímeo ego dóminum meum regem, qui constítuit vobis cibum et potum: qui, si víderit vultus vestros macilentióres præ céteris adolescéntibus coǽvis vestris, condemnábitis caput meum regi.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Aspice, Dómine, quia facta est desoláta cívitas plena divítiis, sedet in tristítia dómina géntium:
* Non est qui consolétur eam, nisi tu, Deus noster.
<r>℣.</r> Plorans plorávit in nocte, et lácrimæ eius in maxíllis eius.
<r>℟.</r> Non est qui consolétur eam, nisi tu, Deus noster.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>Dan 1:5-7</r>
<n>5</n> And the king appointed them a daily provision, of his own meat, and of the wine of which he drank himself, that being nourished three years, afterwards they might stand before the king.
<n>6</n> Now there were among them of the children of Juda, Daniel, Ananias, Misael, and Azarias.
<n>7</n> And the master of the eunuchs gave them names: to Daniel, Baltassar: to Ananias, Sidrach: to Misael, Misach: and to Azarias, Abdenago.
<r>Dan 1:8-10</r>
<n>8</n> But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not be defiled with the king's table, nor with the wine which he drank: and he requested the master of the eunuchs that he might not be defiled.
<n>9</n> And God gave to Daniel grace and mercy in the sight of the prince of the eunuchs.
<n>10</n> And the prince of the eunuchs said to Daniel: I fear my lord the king, who hath appointed you meat and drink: who if he should see your faces leaner than those of the other youths your equals, you shall endanger my head to the king.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Consider, O Lord, how that the city sitteth solitary that was full of riches; how is she become as a widow, she that was great among the nations;

<r>℣.</r> She weepeth sore in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks.
<r>℟.</r> She hath none to comfort her, save thee, O our God.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Matthǽum
<r>Matt 13:24-30</r>
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Dixit Iesus turbis parábolam hanc: Símile factum est regnum cælórum hómini, qui seminávit bonum semen in agro suo. Et réliqua.

Homilía S. Augustíni Epíscopi
<r>Liber Quæst. Evang. in Matth. cap. 11, tom. 4</r>
<c>C</c>um negligéntius ágerent præpósiti Ecclésiæ, aut cum dormitiónem mortis accíperent Apóstoli, venit diábolus, et superseminávit eos, quos malos fílios Dóminus interpretátur. Sed quǽritur: utrum hærétici sint, an male vivéntes cathólici? Possunt enim dici fílii mali étiam hærétici, quia ex eódem Evangélii sémine, et Christi nómine procreáti, pravis opiniónibus ad falsa dógmata convertúntur.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Honor, virtus et potéstas et impérium sit Trinitáti in unitáte, † unitáti in Trinitáte,
* In perénni sæculórum témpore.
<r>℣.</r> Trinitáti lux perénnis, Unitáti sit decus pérpetim.
<r>℟.</r> In perénni sæculórum témpore.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> In perénni sæculórum témpore.

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.
Te ætérnum Patrem * omnis terra venerátur.
Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;
Venerándum tuum verum * et únicum Fílium;
Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.
Tu Rex glóriæ, * Christe.
Tu Patris * sempitérnus es Fílius.
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.
Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
<n>(Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus)</n> Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
<n>(Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem)</n> Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.

<h>Reading 3</h>
From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew
<r>Matt 13:24-30</r>
<c>A</c>t that time, Jesus said to the people a parable: The kingdom of heaven is likened to a man that sowed good seeds in his field. And so on.

Homily by St. Augustine, Bishop <n>of Hippo.</n>
<r>Quest. Evang. Matth. xi, Bk. 4</r>
<c>W</c>hen the Shepherds of the Church wax careless, and since the Apostles sleep the sleep of death, cometh the devil, and soweth them whom the Lord calleth a seed of evil-doers. Now, are these seed of evil-doers the heretics, or Catholics of bad lives?
